title: Character Sheet flow — one supplied image in, a 3-panel sheet out, front full body HEADLESS
description:
Fabio, 2026-08-09: the flow he actually wants. User supplies ONE image; the flow returns a locked character sheet. Three of the four shipped flows are marked for deprecation and only head-swap follows through, so this is the next real flow.

NOT A NEW IDEA ON THE BOARD, BUT NOT A CARD EITHER: 'Character sheet creator - the keystone' is candidate workflow 4 in tasks/MPI-348/brief.md s8, with Fabio's own best-performing layout from past tests (one square image: face SIDE profile, face FRONT profile, FULL BODY). MPI-348's stated working mode is that ideas surfacing mid-authoring become their own cards rather than growing that one, so this is that card. MPI-348 keeps the Krea2 bench track; this card owns the flow.

THE LAYOUT CONFLICTS AND THE CONFLICT IS THE DECISION. Higgsfield's HELL GRIND production brief (95-min AI feature, 15 people, under $500K, 14 days of generation, Cannes Marche du Film 2026) specifies a different sheet, and gives the failure each choice fixes: (a) THREE PANELS - face close-up, full body front, full body back; (b) THE FRONT FULL-BODY FIGURE HAS NO HEAD, because on wide shots the model kept sourcing the face from the tiny blurry full-body figure; remove that head and the model has exactly one place to take the face from, the close-up; (c) the portrait panel is a LARGE 3/4 view (face turned slightly, never straight-on) - 'the sheets the model understands best'; (d) KEEP THE SHEET BORING: neutral grey background, flat light, real skin with visible pores, no retouch, and explicitly NO film grain and NO cinematic lens character baked in, or 'the character will carry that look into every scene and stop reacting to new light'; (e) always check the pupil CATCH-LIGHT, even on dark eyes - without it the face is dead and no video model can act with it; (f) pick the most BELIEVABLE face out of the candidates, never the most beautiful - 'a beautiful but fake face will show its fakeness later, in video, when it is too late to fix'. Fabio's layout (side profile + front profile + full body) and theirs (3/4 close-up + headless front body + back body) are both evidence-backed and differ on every panel. Settle it at the bench before building UI. Note their sheet also serves LoRA training, which is why MPI-348 wanted view/scene count and single-square-vs-separate-images as options.

HARDER THAN THEIR PROBLEM, AND THIS IS THE REAL RISK: Higgsfield generated sheets from a PROMPT in Soul Cinema (a hosted creative model), picking the best of several candidates. Fabio's ask is ONE SUPPLIED IMAGE in - reference-driven, not text-driven, and it must hold identity onto a BACK view the source photo never shows. Nothing on the board proves a local model does that. Prove that single step at the bench before any flow work: Qwen-Edit is documented in MPI-348 s7 as strongest at COMBINING images and weak on single-image instruction edits, which is the wrong half; Krea2 is the single-ref identity path (ref_boost ~4, MPI-348 s8.3); Boogu Image Edit is the fallback. If no local path holds a back view, the flow ships front + 3/4 close-up only and says so.

THE HEADLESS PANEL IS A MASK OP, NOT A PROMPT. Do not ask a model to draw a headless body - generate the front body normally, then SAM3-segment the head (docs/masking-sam3.md, click-point or text branch, sam3.1_multiplex_fp16) and remove it, letting the backdrop fill. klein-4b has a real inpaint op and Cubric Prompt's rules already record that Klein's removal path wants the prompt EMPTY. This also honours the brief's hardest asset rule: 'an image never runs through a model twice in full - every extra pass destroys texture and drifts colour; after two passes the face turns symmetrical, plastic and lifeless, and that dead texture later hurts the acting in video.' Their own point-change workflow (clothes, scars, blood) is the same shape: edit on the sheet, then composite back through a MASK by hand so the original skin texture survives. head-swap already owns that machinery.

STRESS TEST IS PART OF THE DEFINITION OF DONE, not a nice-to-have: ten generations, different poses and different light, recognisable 10 out of 10, and tested NEXT TO the other assets and in the light of the scenes ahead - 'a hero who looks stable alone often breaks when he shares the frame with someone. If the test fails, the problem is your description, not the model.'

ADJACENT, SAME BRIEF, SEPARATE CARDS IF WANTED: the LOCATION sheet (shoot 3/4 never frontal, one anchor object, one light logic, and the reverse-angle trick they found late - generate a VIDEO of the empty location with the camera walking through it, screenshot the angle, then texture-clean it: a full location sheet out of a single image, which Vision can already do end to end), and the ASSET REGISTRY (an asset is a PAIR - image plus a descriptor that goes into every prompt word for word; every STATE is its own asset, @roco/@roco_wet/@roco_blood, because mixing states in one text makes the model mix them between shots).

SOURCES: full distillation in ~/.claude/memory/domain/ai-video-asset-production.md. Raw material saved at C:\Users\Fabio\Downloads\seedance_skills\ - 'HELL GRIND project brief (extracted).txt' plus the CINEDANCE, ACTING and LIRA skill files. The recipe/enhancer half of the same brief is Cubric Prompt's MPI-28.
